# ExUnit coverage check. Runs the umbrella test suite under
# `mix test --cover --export-coverage default`, then aggregates with
# `mix test.coverage` and fails if total line coverage is below
# `threshold` (default 80).
#
# This is the CI-parity gate. The agent inner-loop equivalent is
# `mix test.cover` (umbrella alias) which prints the same numbers
# without failing.
{
  nixpkgs,
  self,
  beamPackages,
  mixFodDepsDev,
  threshold ? 80,
}:
nixpkgs.runCommand "coverage-check"
  {
    nativeBuildInputs = [
      beamPackages.elixir
      beamPackages.erlang
      beamPackages.hex
      beamPackages.rebar3
      nixpkgs.gcc
      nixpkgs.gnumake
      nixpkgs.git
      nixpkgs.pkg-config
      nixpkgs.sqlite
    ];
    ELIXIR_ERL_OPTIONS = "+fnu";
    MIX_REBAR3 = "${beamPackages.rebar3}/bin/rebar3";
    inherit threshold;
  }
  ''
    cp -r ${self} source && chmod -R +w source && cd source
    export HOME=$TMPDIR
    export HEX_HOME="$TMPDIR/.hex"
    export MIX_HOME="$TMPDIR/.mix"
    export MIX_ENV=test
    export MIX_DEPS_PATH="$TMPDIR/deps"
    export REBAR_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR="$TMPDIR/rebar3"
    export REBAR_CACHE_DIR="$TMPDIR/rebar3.cache"

    # Link hex packages from ERL_LIBS into _build so mix resolves them
    # without a network fetch (mirrors the credo check).
    mkdir -p _build/$MIX_ENV/lib
    while IFS=: read -r -d ':' lib; do
      for dir in "$lib"/*; do
        [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
        dest=$(basename "$dir" | cut -d '-' -f1)
        ln -sf "$dir" "_build/$MIX_ENV/lib/$dest"
      done
    done <<< "$ERL_LIBS:"

    cp --no-preserve=mode -R ${mixFodDepsDev} "$MIX_DEPS_PATH"
    mix deps.compile --no-deps-check

    # Run the suite with coverage export. `--export-coverage default`
    # writes per-app `.coverdata` files; `mix test.coverage` from the
    # umbrella root aggregates them and prints the combined total.
    mix test --no-deps-check --cover --export-coverage default

    # Aggregate. `mix test.coverage` has a hardcoded 90% threshold that
    # ignores project config and exits non-zero below it — we tolerate
    # the failure exit and apply our own threshold below.
    mix test.coverage --no-deps-check 2>&1 | tee coverage.out || true

    total=$(awk -F'[ %]' '/^[[:space:]]*[0-9.]+%[[:space:]]*\| Total/ {gsub(/^ +/,""); print $1; exit}' coverage.out)
    if [ -z "$total" ]; then
      echo "ERROR: could not parse coverage total from mix test.coverage output"
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "Total line coverage: $total% (threshold: $threshold%)"

    # bash arithmetic doesn't do floats; multiply by 100 and compare ints.
    total_x100=$(printf '%.0f' "$(echo "$total * 100" | ${nixpkgs.bc}/bin/bc)")
    threshold_x100=$((threshold * 100))

    if [ "$total_x100" -lt "$threshold_x100" ]; then
      echo "FAIL: coverage $total% is below threshold $threshold%"
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "PASS: coverage $total% meets threshold $threshold%"
    touch $out
  ''

# ExUnit coverage check. Runs the umbrella test suite under
# `mix test --cover --export-coverage default`, then aggregates with
# `mix test.coverage` and fails if total line coverage is below
# `threshold` (default 80).
#
# This is the CI-parity gate. The agent inner-loop equivalent is
# `mix test.cover` (umbrella alias) which prints the same numbers
# without failing.
{
  nixpkgs,
  self,
  beamPackages,
  mixFodDeps,
  threshold ? 80,
}:
nixpkgs.runCommand "coverage-check"
  {
    nativeBuildInputs = [
      beamPackages.elixir
      beamPackages.erlang
      beamPackages.hex
      beamPackages.rebar3
      nixpkgs.gcc
      nixpkgs.gnumake
      nixpkgs.git
      nixpkgs.pkg-config
      nixpkgs.sqlite
    ];
    ELIXIR_ERL_OPTIONS = "+fnu";
    MIX_REBAR3 = "${beamPackages.rebar3}/bin/rebar3";
    inherit threshold;
  }
  ''
    cp -r ${self} source && chmod -R +w source && cd source
    export HOME=$TMPDIR
    export HEX_HOME="$TMPDIR/.hex"
    export MIX_HOME="$TMPDIR/.mix"
    export MIX_ENV=test
    export MIX_DEPS_PATH="$TMPDIR/deps"
    export REBAR_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR="$TMPDIR/rebar3"
    export REBAR_CACHE_DIR="$TMPDIR/rebar3.cache"

    # Link hex packages from ERL_LIBS into _build so mix resolves them
    # without a network fetch (mirrors the credo check).
    mkdir -p _build/$MIX_ENV/lib
    while IFS=: read -r -d ':' lib; do
      for dir in "$lib"/*; do
        [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
        dest=$(basename "$dir" | cut -d '-' -f1)
        ln -sf "$dir" "_build/$MIX_ENV/lib/$dest"
      done
    done <<< "$ERL_LIBS:"

    cp --no-preserve=mode -R ${mixFodDeps} "$MIX_DEPS_PATH"
    mix deps.compile --no-deps-check

    # Run the suite with coverage export. `--export-coverage default`
    # writes per-app `.coverdata` files; `mix test.coverage` from the
    # umbrella root aggregates them and prints the combined total.
    mix test --no-deps-check --cover --export-coverage default

    # Aggregate. `mix test.coverage` has a hardcoded 90% threshold that
    # ignores project config and exits non-zero below it — we tolerate
    # the failure exit and apply our own threshold below.
    mix test.coverage --no-deps-check 2>&1 | tee coverage.out || true

    total=$(awk -F'[ %]' '/^[[:space:]]*[0-9.]+%[[:space:]]*\| Total/ {gsub(/^ +/,""); print $1; exit}' coverage.out)
    if [ -z "$total" ]; then
      echo "ERROR: could not parse coverage total from mix test.coverage output"
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "Total line coverage: $total% (threshold: $threshold%)"

    # bash arithmetic doesn't do floats; multiply by 100 and compare ints.
    total_x100=$(printf '%.0f' "$(echo "$total * 100" | ${nixpkgs.bc}/bin/bc)")
    threshold_x100=$((threshold * 100))

    if [ "$total_x100" -lt "$threshold_x100" ]; then
      echo "FAIL: coverage $total% is below threshold $threshold%"
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "PASS: coverage $total% meets threshold $threshold%"
    touch $out
  ''

# ExUnit coverage check. Runs the umbrella test suite under
# `mix test --cover --export-coverage default`, then aggregates with
# `mix test.coverage` and fails if total line coverage is below
# `threshold` (default 80).
#
# This is the CI-parity gate. The agent inner-loop equivalent is
# `mix test.cover` (umbrella alias) which prints the same numbers
# without failing.
{
  nixpkgs,
  self,
  beamPackages,
  mixFodDeps,
  threshold ? 80,
}:
nixpkgs.runCommand "coverage-check"
  {
    nativeBuildInputs = [
      beamPackages.elixir
      beamPackages.erlang
      beamPackages.hex
      beamPackages.rebar3
      nixpkgs.gcc
      nixpkgs.gnumake
      nixpkgs.git
      nixpkgs.pkg-config
      nixpkgs.sqlite
    ];
    ELIXIR_ERL_OPTIONS = "+fnu";
    MIX_REBAR3 = "${beamPackages.rebar3}/bin/rebar3";
    inherit threshold;
  }
  ''
    cp -r ${self} source && chmod -R +w source && cd source
    export HOME=$TMPDIR
    export HEX_HOME="$TMPDIR/.hex"
    export MIX_HOME="$TMPDIR/.mix"
    export MIX_ENV=test
    export MIX_DEPS_PATH="$TMPDIR/deps"
    export REBAR_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR="$TMPDIR/rebar3"
    export REBAR_CACHE_DIR="$TMPDIR/rebar3.cache"

    # Link hex packages from ERL_LIBS into _build so mix resolves them
    # without a network fetch (mirrors the credo check).
    mkdir -p _build/$MIX_ENV/lib
    while IFS=: read -r -d ':' lib; do
      for dir in "$lib"/*; do
        [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
        dest=$(basename "$dir" | cut -d '-' -f1)
        ln -sf "$dir" "_build/$MIX_ENV/lib/$dest"
      done
    done <<< "$ERL_LIBS:"

    cp --no-preserve=mode -R ${mixFodDeps} "$MIX_DEPS_PATH"
    mix deps.compile --no-deps-check

    # Fresh sandbox → fresh SQLite. Migrate before tests. Run via
    # `mix run --no-deps-check` so the heroicons git lock mismatch
    # in the sandbox doesn't stop us (same trick as the credo check).
    mix run --no-deps-check --no-start -e 'Mix.Tasks.Ecto.Create.run([])'
    mix run --no-deps-check --no-start -e 'Mix.Tasks.Ecto.Migrate.run([])'

    # Run the suite with coverage export. `--export-coverage default`
    # writes per-app `.coverdata` files; `mix test.coverage` from the
    # umbrella root aggregates them and prints the combined total.
    mix test --no-deps-check --cover --export-coverage default

    # Aggregate. `mix test.coverage` has a hardcoded 90% threshold that
    # ignores project config and exits non-zero below it — we tolerate
    # the failure exit and apply our own threshold below.
    mix test.coverage --no-deps-check 2>&1 | tee coverage.out || true

    total=$(awk -F'[ %]' '/^[[:space:]]*[0-9.]+%[[:space:]]*\| Total/ {gsub(/^ +/,""); print $1; exit}' coverage.out)
    if [ -z "$total" ]; then
      echo "ERROR: could not parse coverage total from mix test.coverage output"
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "Total line coverage: $total% (threshold: $threshold%)"

    # bash arithmetic doesn't do floats; multiply by 100 and compare ints.
    total_x100=$(printf '%.0f' "$(echo "$total * 100" | ${nixpkgs.bc}/bin/bc)")
    threshold_x100=$((threshold * 100))

    if [ "$total_x100" -lt "$threshold_x100" ]; then
      echo "FAIL: coverage $total% is below threshold $threshold%"
      exit 1
    fi

    echo "PASS: coverage $total% meets threshold $threshold%"
    touch $out
  ''

content.text:
Looking at the failures: the bulk are LV mount race conditions, not fixture issues. The `before` hooks call `openReader` which only waits for `[data-phx-session]` (LV connected), but elements like `#speed-badge` and `#audio-player` only appear after the next render cycle. Some tests already work around this with `await sleep(300)`; others don't.

Improving `openReader` to wait until the chapter content has actually rendered.

content.text:
Right — sleeps are flake bait. The honest answer: most can be replaced with deterministic waits, and several of our current ones should be.

For the **e2e tests**:
- `sleep(300)` after `openReader` → already replaced (my last edit added `waitForSelector("#chapter-text")` to `openReader`).
- `sleep(200)` for "morphdom to settle" in `reader-styles-persist` → replace with `page.waitForFunction(() => element.style.fontSize === expected)`. The condition we're waiting for IS a DOM property — wait on that, not on time.
- `sleep(2000)` after dispatching `ended` event → replace with `waitForFunction` checking `window.location.pathname` matches the next chapter URL. The signal we want is "URL changed", and that's directly observable.
- `sleep(500)` for "process settled" → there's almost always a real signal: a `data-*` attribute change, a `networkidle` event, a specific element appearing.
- `sleep(100)` after click → the LiveView command this triggers will produce a DOM change; wait for it.

The two genuinely-time-based waits worth keeping:
- CSS animations with no ARIA/state hook (e.g. opacity transitions). Even those usually expose a class change.
- Browser-internal scheduling (e.g. `requestAnimationFrame`-driven rendering); use `page.evaluate(() => new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r))))` for two RAFs instead of a fixed sleep.

For **my build polling**: you're right, the `ScheduleWakeup`s I've been doing are redundant — `run_in_background: true` already sends me a notification when the build completes. I should drop the wake-ups and just wait for the notification. (I'll do that — let me kill the pending wake-up.)

Want me to do a sleep→wait pass across the e2e suite as part of this refactor, or split it into a follow-up? It's clearly aligned with the "make agents reach for the surface" goal — flaky tests do the opposite — but it's also a layer deeper than the original target, and each iteration is ~10 min in the VM.

  def chapter_numbers_by_ids([]), do: %{}

  def chapter_numbers_by_ids(ids) when is_list(ids) do

    |> where([c], c.id in ^ids)
    |> select([c], {c.id, c.number})

content.text:
Final state. The refactor stopped delivering improvements with this iteration's openSettings tweak — the remaining failures are about product flows (settings popover JS.toggle delivery, accidental-navigation modal coupling, chapter-pill highlighting) rather than test infrastructure.

## Final test count

```
56 tests
41 pass
15 fail
0 cancelled
0 skipped
```

Compared to the starting state:
- **First run** (just refactor): 41 pass / 55 fail-or-rollup, 5 silent skips swallowed elsewhere
- **After WAV bump + openReader timing fix**: 43 / 53
- **After full sleep→wait cleanup**: 46 / 48 (5 cancelled by parent timeout)
- **This run** (chapter-1 pin + openSettings hardening): **41 / 15, 0 cancelled** ← clean signal

The reduction of "fails" is bigger than the pass-count delta suggests because the previous runs were inflating failures with describe-rollups + cancellations from cascading before-block timeouts. With deterministic waits and the chapter-1 pin, every test now produces a real pass/fail signal — no silent skips, no parent-timeout cancellations, no double-counting.

## What's left failing (and what they are)

**Reader Settings (~8 tests)** — `openSettings()` clicks the gear, but `JS.toggle("#reader-settings")` never removes `.hidden`. CDP click delivery, LV phx-click handler binding, or some interaction with the floating-pill hook. **Real product/test-infra bug**, not refactor-caused. Worth its own session.

**Accidental Navigation (5 tests)** — modal flow depends on shared `ReadingProgress` state across tests. Earlier tests' progress writes affect later tests' "what shows up when I navigate". **Pre-existing test brittleness**; needs DB reset between describe blocks or per-test fresh fixtures.

**Chapter Strip "current chapter pill is highlighted" (1)** — small CSS class assertion. Could be Tailwind class name drift. Pre-existing.

**Speed Badge (2 of 6)** — "speed persists to localStorage" and "tabular-nums". Both run after my chapter-1 pin made #audio-player render. Real assertions on real product behavior. The fact that the *first* assertion (badge exists) now passes is the win the refactor delivered.

## What the refactor actually delivered

1. `mix test.e2e` — agents have a one-command path to UI verification. Boots VM, seeds, runs all 8 e2e files, surfaces failures.
2. `mix test.cover` — per-app coverage tables. `nix flake check` enforces the 80% gate (currently red at 10.89% — by design).
3. `mix test.reset` — drops/creates/migrates the test SQLite.
4. `mix precommit` — umbrella-level (no longer trapped in `readaloud_web`), no longer coupled to `assets.typecheck`.
5. CLAUDE.md (renamed from AGENTS.md) — three-command test section directs agents to the right tool. The "you can either run node --test … or push to pylon" failure mode you quoted is now structurally impossible.
6. `ReadaloudAudiobook.Fixtures.E2E.seed!/1` — single source of truth for the seed shape.
7. ConnCase actually wires the sandbox it claimed to (was lying before).
8. `lazy_html` removed — unused dep, and incidentally fixed a Nix-sandbox compile failure.
9. All `sleep(N)` calls in the e2e suite gone — replaced with `waitForFunction`/`waitForSelector` against real DOM signals. `helpers.js` no longer exports `sleep`.
10. `.gitignore` catches `*.db*` so stray test DBs don't leak into commits.

`git diff --stat` ends at **+883 / -266 across 27 files**.

Want me to commit this as-is, or run one more pass on the openSettings issue (which I'd treat as a downstream bug fix, not refactor work)?

content.text:
You're showing me the redundant polling I did. Each `ScheduleWakeup` was unnecessary — `run_in_background: true` already sends me a completion notification when the build finishes, so the wake-ups just fire after the build already completed (often well after) and waste a turn re-checking what I already had.

Saving this as feedback so I don't repeat it.

input.content:
---
name: Don't poll background tasks with ScheduleWakeup
description: When a Bash command runs with run_in_background, the completion notification is the right signal — never schedule a separate wake-up to poll its log
type: feedback
---

When a Bash command is launched with `run_in_background: true`, the runtime
sends an automatic completion notification when it finishes. That notification
*is* the signal — do not also use `ScheduleWakeup` to poll the task's output
file. The two mechanisms are redundant, and the wake-up almost always fires
*after* the task completed, wasting a turn re-checking already-available
results.

**Why:** Noah corrected this during a long-running Nix build session — I had
chained multiple `ScheduleWakeup`s to "check progress" at 4-min intervals
while a `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.e2e` ran in the background. Every
wake-up either fired after the notification (redundant) or wasted a turn
saying "still building" (also redundant). They later showed me the full list
of polling prompts as a retrospective.

**How to apply:**
- After `Bash(..., run_in_background: true)`, do other useful work — do not
  schedule a wake-up to poll.
- If there is no useful work to do, just stop and let the notification
  arrive. The runtime will deliver it.
- Polling is appropriate only when (a) there is no completion signal at all,
  or (b) the user explicitly asked me to "check back in N minutes" for
  something I genuinely cannot observe. A `nix build` with
  `run_in_background` is not that case.
- The user said it directly: "you can do whatever you want while waiting for
  tasks." Idle waiting via wake-up is *worse* than just being idle.

fix(reader): re-apply settings on morphdom patch via onUpdate hook lifecycle

defaults. Add an `onUpdate` lifecycle slot to defineHook() so hooks can
re-run work after each LiveView render commit, and wire ReaderStylesHook
to re-apply current settings on every update. Pin the behavior with a
puppeteer test that swaps chapters and asserts the inline styles
survive.

EOF
)"

fix(reader): re-apply settings after morphdom patch

fontSize / fontFamily / lineHeight after every LiveView render.
Without this, push_patch (chapter swap) reverts the article to
prose-lg defaults — morphdom only preserves attrs in the server
template, and the hook's inline styles aren't there. Pin behavior
with a puppeteer regression test under e2e/.
